# Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 36 (Bu-Vb Pc36)

**ID:** Bu-Vb Pc36  
**Section:** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga (bu-vb)  
**Collection:** Vinaya  
**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 36  
**Title (English, from literature):** Encouraging a monastic to eat after refusing an invitation  
**tipitaka.org (CST):** [https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m1.mul0.xml](https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m1.mul0.xml)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Dutiyapavāraṇā Sikkhāpada* ("The Second Training Rule on Refusal/Invitation") constitutes the thirty-sixth rule in the *Pācittiya* chapter of the Theravāda *Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga*. According to the rule, a monk commits an offense requiring confession if he entices or tricks another monk—who has already completed his meal and refused further offers of food—into eating more, with the deliberate aim of finding fault with or criticizing him. As noted in comparative Vinaya analysis, this monastic regulation directly refers back to the situation governed by the preceding rule (*Pācittiya* 35) [Hüsken 1997].
